narrativeReportMd:
# Specimen R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. The R6 Specimen resource keeps the same canonical identity, but several populated R4 elements are not valid R6 without transformation: `accessionIdentifier` is folded into typed `identifier`, `container` is remodeled around required `device[x]`, `processing.procedure` is renamed to `processing.method`, and `collection.bodySite` plus `processing.additive` change to `CodeableReference` wire shapes.

## Scope
I analyzed the base R4 and R6 Specimen StructureDefinitions and supporting local terminology files. Inherited differences from Element, Extension, Resource, DomainResource, BackboneElement, and datatype infrastructure are excluded except where Specimen locally changes the datatype used at a Specimen path.

## Main migration themes
The largest theme is representation normalization: R6 moves accession identifiers into typed identifiers, container facts into device/device-definition modeling, and coded-or-referenced concepts into CodeableReference. A second theme is richer workflow semantics: subject/focus disambiguation, collection Procedure linkage, device/performer fields, and role/feature/combined metadata improve expressivity but complicate R6-to-R4 downgrade.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact hard breaks are the removal/merge of `accessionIdentifier`, the container remodel with mandatory `container.device[x]`, the `processing.procedure` to `processing.method` rename, `collection.bodySite` becoming CodeableReference, and `processing.additive` becoming CodeableReference. These affect validation, generated classes, FHIRPath paths, and cross-version transforms.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for container migration, processing terminology mapping, subject-versus-focus semantics, and deciding how to preserve R6-only workflow and specimen-characterization fields when exporting to R4.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many changes appear justified by better modeling, but several could have been phased in less disruptively with deprecated aliases or optional sibling fields. The R6-to-R4 representability risks are mostly inherent to new optional expressivity.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate base-artifact reports should handle inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element changes. Cross-version ConceptMaps or official migration guidance would materially improve confidence for container-to-Device and processing procedure-to-method mappings.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Specimen` has material R4->R6 breaking changes despite stable artifact identity. The top migration concerns are the container remodel with required `device[x]`, CodeableReference wire-shape changes for body site/additive, and the accession/processing path changes. The main uncertainty is not whether the structural breaks exist, but how official guidance intends legacy container and processing terminology to map.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration needs explicit transforms for removed or renamed properties (`accessionIdentifier`, container children, `processing.procedure`) and structural wrapping for CodeableReference paths. R6 also adds richer semantics (`focus`, `combined`, `role`, `feature`, Procedure/device/performer workflow fields) that should be preserved with extensions or accepted loss when downgrading to R4. Validators and generated models must be regenerated rather than reused because several same-looking paths now expose different datatypes.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level element presence, cardinality, type, target, binding-strength, and invariant findings because both primary StructureDefinitions were available and compared directly. Confidence is medium for terminology/rationale details where SNOMED expansions, official diffs, and cross-version ConceptMaps were not available in the supplied inputs.

findings.title: Specimen.accessionIdentifier was removed and folded into Specimen.identifier

oldState.summary: R4 had a distinct optional accession identifier element.

semanticText.definition: The identifier assigned by the lab when accessioning specimen(s). This is not necessarily the same as the specimen identifier, depending on local lab procedures.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, accession number semantics had their own `Specimen.accessionIdentifier` slot separate from the repeating specimen `identifier` list.

newState.summary: R6 has no accessionIdentifier element; accession identifiers are represented as typed entries in Specimen.identifier.

semanticText.definition: Identifiers used for specimen identification. These could include but are not limited to identifiers generated upon collection, accessioning, or other reasons for labeling a specimen.
semanticText.comment: For accession identifiers, the Accession Identifier code, ACSN, should be used in the Identifier.type.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps all specimen business identifiers in `Specimen.identifier` and relies on `Identifier.type` with ACSN to distinguish accession identifiers.

facts.note: Removed from the R6 differential and snapshot.
Inferred from the R6 Specimen.identifier comment.
Replacement lives in the repeating identifier array.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `Specimen.identifier` definition explicitly includes accessioning identifiers and its comment names `Identifier.type` code `ACSN` as the accession representation, so this is best treated as a merge rather than a simple deletion.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `accessionIdentifier` is old-valid/new-invalid because R6 no longer defines that property. Generated R4 models and database columns that expose a dedicated accession field also need code changes. R6-to-R4 conversion is possible only when the accession identifier can be selected reliably from `Specimen.identifier`, usually by `Identifier.type` = `ACSN`; otherwise multiple identifiers become ambiguous.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Accession identifiers are operationally important in laboratory workflows; losing or misclassifying them can break specimen tracking and result reconciliation.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify all specimen business identifiers in one repeating Identifier element and distinguish accession numbers by Identifier.type.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `accessionIdentifier` as a deprecated alias while recommending ACSN-typed entries in `identifier`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of consolidating specimen business identifiers under `identifier` with `Identifier.type = ACSN` is reasonable. A less-breaking base design could have kept the old element temporarily, but that would leave duplicate accession-number representations in the same resource. Given that material interoperability tradeoff, the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking option would keep `Specimen.accessionIdentifier` optional and deprecated while documenting ACSN-typed `Specimen.identifier` as preferred. That preserves R4 wire compatibility and supports gradual migration, but it also requires rules for conflicts between `accessionIdentifier` and `identifier[]` and creates a risk that both representations remain in use indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances, but keeps two same-resource locations for accession identifiers and risks inconsistent or indefinite dual use.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Specimen.accessionIdentifier` as `Identifier` with cardinality 0..1 and summary=true.
No R6 element with id `Specimen.accessionIdentifier` exists.
R6 states that accession identifiers should be represented using `Identifier.type` code ACSN.
evidence.quote: For accession identifiers, the Accession Identifier code, ACSN, should be used in the Identifier.type.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative and omit unrelated fields. The migration keeps the same identifier value but moves it into the repeating `identifier` array with an accession type code.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 had a dedicated `Specimen.accessionIdentifier`; R6 removes it and points implementers to typed `Specimen.identifier` entries. This is a direct wire-format break for any R4 specimen that carries an accession number in the old field, and it is also a code-generation break for clients with an accession-specific property.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 JSON containing `accessionIdentifier` will not validate as a base R6 Specimen. R6 data can be converted back only if a converter can identify which `identifier` entry is the accession identifier; `Identifier.type` = `ACSN` is the intended signal but may be absent in real data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move `accessionIdentifier` into `identifier[]`, preserve `system`, `value`, `assigner`, `period`, and add or preserve `Identifier.type` coding `ACSN` when appropriate. Test cases should include specimens with both R4 `identifier` and `accessionIdentifier` so duplicate handling and ordering are deterministic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation is understandable because `Identifier.type` can express accession semantics without a special field. It was not fully backward compatible; retaining the old element as deprecated for one release would have made old instances valid while still allowing the new representation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had a distinct `accessionIdentifier` slot, while R6 folds accession numbers into repeating `identifier` entries marked with `Identifier.type = ACSN`. That is a real old-valid/new-invalid wire break for specimens that carry accession numbers and it can affect lab tracking models, but the migration is usually mechanical and the R6 design avoids maintaining two first-class accession fields with conflict rules.
keyEvidence: R4 `StructureDefinition-Specimen.json` defines `Specimen.accessionIdentifier` as `Identifier` 0..1.
R6 has no `Specimen.accessionIdentifier`; `Specimen.identifier.comment` says accession identifiers should use Identifier.type code ACSN.
R4 metadata checked: Specimen FMM 2 and standards status trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral: it does not create a strong stability presumption, but accession identifiers are operationally important enough that the hard wire break still matters.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with `accessionIdentifier` uses an element R6 no longer defines; generated models also lose the dedicated property.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A deprecated `accessionIdentifier` alias could have preserved old instances, but it would leave two same-resource places for the same accession number and require precedence or synchronization rules. That tradeoff makes the R6 consolidation proportionate.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the hard break is real, but I would not treat the alias option as low-cost enough to require redesign.

findings.title: Specimen.container was remodeled: several R4 subelements were removed and R6 requires container.device[x]

oldState.summary: R4 container carried inline identifier, description, type, capacity, specimenQuantity, and additive[x].
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented many container facts directly under `Specimen.container`, including `identifier`, `description`, `type`, `capacity`, and `additive[x]`; none of those children was mandatory.

newState.summary: R6 container retains specimenQuantity but requires `device[x]` 1..1 and removes the former inline container details.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, each container backbone must contain exactly one `device[x]`, represented as a `CodeableConcept`, `Reference(Device)`, or canonical `DeviceDefinition`; the former inline container identifier, description, type, capacity, and additive are absent.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The parent backbone path remains `Specimen.container`, but the child model changes from inline descriptive fields to a required device reference/code. This is a local content-model replacement, not an inherited backbone change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance using removed container children is old-valid/new-invalid. Even an R4 container that only carried `specimenQuantity` cannot become a valid R6 container without supplying the new required `device[x]`. R6 containers that use `Reference(Device)` or canonical `DeviceDefinition` cannot be represented cleanly in R4's inline container fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Container identifiers, type, additives, and capacity are commonly used for specimen handling; an incorrect transform can affect chain-of-custody, pre-analytic interpretation, and container-specific processing rules.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize container representation around Device/DeviceDefinition so container facts can be managed as device-like artifacts rather than repeated inline fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add optional `container.device[x]` while retaining the R4 inline container children as deprecated transition fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing containers around `Device` or `DeviceDefinition` is a plausible R6 goal, especially for reusable device identity and richer device metadata. The less-breaking design is real, but it is incomplete for that goal because old inline fields and new device references could disagree and would need long-term reconciliation. Those material tradeoffs make the breaking remodel probably justified, even though the mandatory `device[x]` requirement is harsh for legacy container-only instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatible base design could have made `container.device[x]` optional and kept `identifier`, `description`, `type`, `capacity`, and `additive[x]` on `Specimen.container` with deprecation guidance. This would allow most R4 instances to validate unchanged while encouraging migration to device-based modeling. The cost is persistent duplication, validation ambiguity over which representation is authoritative, and extra implementation burden for systems that must compare or synchronize inline fields with referenced device content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve legacy containers, but creates competing inline-vs-device representations for the same container facts and weakens normalization.

evidence.detail: R4 defines container identifiers as `Identifier` 0..*.
R4 defines container type as `CodeableConcept` 0..1 bound to specimen-container-type.
R4 defines container capacity as `SimpleQuantity` 0..1.
R4 defines container additive as `CodeableConcept` or `Reference(Substance)` 0..1.
R6 adds mandatory `Specimen.container.device[x]` with cardinality 1..1 and types CodeableConcept, Reference(Device), canonical(DeviceDefinition).

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows only the simplest case where an old `type` text can seed `deviceCodeableConcept`. Old container identifiers, capacity, and additives may require a `Device`, `DeviceDefinition`, or extension to avoid loss.

findings.narrativeMd: `Specimen.container` is the largest local remodel. R4 represented container facts inline; R6 makes the container point to or code a device and requires that device whenever the container backbone is present. This means old container-bearing instances need an active transform, not just a schema version bump.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 properties such as `container.identifier`, `container.type`, `container.capacity`, and `container.additive[x]` are unknown in R6. Separately, R6 requires `container.device[x]` with `min=1`, so a converted container without a device value fails validation. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for Device/DeviceDefinition identity and for device-level attributes not present in R4 Specimen.container.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map old `container.type` to `container.deviceCodeableConcept` when a code or text is sufficient. For real container instances, create or reference `Device`; for catalog-level container definitions, use canonical `DeviceDefinition` where appropriate. Decide how to carry old container identifiers, capacity, and additives, because R6 Specimen no longer has direct fields for them. Regression tests should cover containers with each removed child and containers with only `specimenQuantity`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change likely supports a more consistent device model, but the mandatory `device[x]` and removal of old fields make it avoidably harsh for legacy data. Optional `device[x]` plus deprecated inline children would have allowed gradual migration. The tradeoff would have been ambiguity about which representation is authoritative.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R6 container backbone keeps the parent path but removes R4 inline container facts such as identifiers, type, capacity, description, and additive, while making `container.device[x]` mandatory. A legacy specimen with container details, or even one with only `specimenQuantity`, needs a nontrivial device-based transform before it can validate. Because containers are central to specimen handling, this looks harsher than necessary for a trial-use/FMM 2 resource.
keyEvidence: R4 defines `Specimen.container.identifier`, `description`, `type`, `capacity`, `specimenQuantity`, and `additive[x]`, all optional.
R6 defines `Specimen.container.device[x]` as 1..1 CodeableConcept, Reference(Device), or canonical(DeviceDefinition), and retains only `specimenQuantity` from the old inline details.
R4 metadata checked: Specimen FMM 2 and standards status trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral rather than strongly protective, but the affected path is a practical lab specimen-handling surface, so the compatibility burden remains material.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: removed child elements are unknown in R6, and each R6 container now requires a `device[x]` value that old instances did not need.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have added optional `device[x]` while deprecating the old inline children for a transition release, or at least avoided making `device[x]` mandatory. That would create duplicate inline-vs-device representations, but the current design invalidates common legacy container records and forces device modeling before validation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment, but disagree with treating the remodel as probably justified; the required device plus removed inline fields merits renewed design attention.

findings.title: Specimen.processing.procedure was replaced by Specimen.processing.method with a different example value set

oldState.summary: R4 used `processing.procedure` as an optional CodeableConcept for the processing procedure.

binding.description: Type indicating the technique used to process the specimen.

semanticText.definition: A coded value specifying the procedure used to process the specimen.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4's processing treatment code was named `procedure` and used the `specimen-processing-procedure` example value set, which includes HL7 v2 table 0373.

newState.summary: R6 uses `processing.method` as an optional CodeableConcept for the processing method.

binding.description: Type indicating the technique used to process the specimen.

semanticText.definition: A coded value specifying the method used to process the specimen.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 changes the element name to `method` and changes the example value set to SNOMED CT descendants of 9265001 according to the local ValueSet.

facts.note: Example bindings do not by themselves make codes invalid, but they affect guidance and mapping.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The cardinality, type, short text, and binding description are nearly the same, while the definition changes from 'procedure' to 'method'. The old element is absent and the new one is present in the same backbone position.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance with `processing.procedure` uses a property that is not defined in R6. Generated classes, FHIRPath expressions, database columns, and profile constraints referencing `.procedure` must be updated to `.method`. R6-to-R4 can often rename back, but the example value set changed from HL7 v2 table 0373 to a SNOMED-based set, so terminology-preserving conversion is not guaranteed.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Processing method affects specimen preparation interpretation, such as fixation or centrifugation, so losing it can affect downstream result interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that the element captures a processing method/technique rather than a full Procedure event, leaving Procedure references to other workflow elements.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `processing.procedure` and clarify its definition, aliases, and binding to indicate a processing method or technique.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of clarifying that this element is a specimen-processing method rather than a full `Procedure` event is reasonable. However, the old path could have been retained with clearer definitions, aliases, and terminology guidance, avoiding a JSON property rename while still communicating the intended meaning. Because that alternative preserves old instances without adding a duplicate base field, the rename appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 design would leave the element at `Specimen.processing.procedure`, update the short/definition to say it records the processing method or technique, and add aliases or explanatory text to discourage confusion with the `Procedure` resource. That alternative does not fully improve the name, but living with a nonoptimal R4 name is a moderate long-term tradeoff compared with invalidating all populated R4 `processing.procedure` instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances with only the moderate cost of retaining a less precise legacy element name.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `processing.procedure` as CodeableConcept 0..1.
No R6 element with id `Specimen.processing.procedure` exists.
R6 defines `processing.method` as CodeableConcept 0..1.
R4 example binding includes HL7 v2-0373; R6 example binding includes SNOMED CT descendants of 9265001.

examples.examplesMd: A text-only CodeableConcept can be mechanically renamed. Coded values need terminology review if preserving code systems matters.

findings.narrativeMd: The processing treatment element was renamed from `procedure` to `method`. This is a high-confidence local rename with a terminology-guidance change; it is hard-breaking at the JSON property level even though the conceptual content is similar.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `processing.procedure` content is old-valid/new-invalid because R6 does not define that child. R6 `processing.method` is not accepted by R4. Code generators and FHIRPath rules must update property names, and terminology-aware systems should not assume every old v2-0373 code has a SNOMED method equivalent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `processing.procedure` to `processing.method`. Preserve CodeableConcept text and codings, but run a terminology review if the implementation expects values from the R6 example SNOMED-based value set. Profile authors should update constraints, search extraction, and transforms referencing the old path.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rename is probably intended to avoid conflating a coded technique with a Procedure event, but it could have been introduced as an additive alias first. A warning invariant would have supported transition without invalidating old instances immediately.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Specimen.processing.procedure` became `Specimen.processing.method` with the same cardinality and datatype, plus a changed example value set. This is a classic same-concept property rename: old JSON, profiles, FHIRPath, generated models, and storage columns all have to move even though R6 could have clarified the old element text and binding guidance in place.
keyEvidence: R4 defines `Specimen.processing.procedure` as CodeableConcept 0..1 with example ValueSet `specimen-processing-procedure`.
R6 omits `processing.procedure` and defines `Specimen.processing.method` as CodeableConcept 0..1 with example ValueSet `specimen-processing-method`.
Local ValueSet check: R4 processing procedure includes HL7 v2-0373; R6 processing method includes SNOMED CT descendants of 9265001.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use does not by itself require old names forever, but it also does not justify an avoidable wire rename when the old path could carry the clarified semantics.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: populated R4 `processing.procedure` is an undefined R6 child; runtime/API/codegen references to the old property also break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `processing.procedure` and revising the short/definition/aliases to say processing method would preserve old instances without adding a duplicate field. The tradeoff is living with a less precise legacy name, which is modest compared with the migration burden.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Yes/probably avoidable alternative judgment.

findings.title: Specimen.collection.bodySite changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(BodyStructure)

oldState.summary: R4 bodySite was a CodeableConcept 0..1 with an example body-site binding.

binding.description: Codes describing anatomical locations. May include laterality.

semanticText.comment: If the use case requires BodySite to be handled as a separate resource instead of an inline coded element then use the standard extension bodySite.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed only an inline coded body site in the base element, with separate-resource use delegated to an extension.

newState.summary: R6 bodySite is a CodeableReference 0..1 targeting BodyStructure, still with an example body-site binding for the concept arm.

semanticText.comment: Reasons for using BodyStructure reference include identifying a specific site instance, lack of a single pre-coordinated code, or representing bodySite using multiple attributes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits either a concept or a reference to a BodyStructure instance, but the wire shape is the CodeableReference datatype rather than a raw CodeableConcept.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path, cardinality, and conceptual meaning remain body-site collection location, but the datatype changed to CodeableReference, which changes JSON/XML shape and adds a reference arm.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A populated R4 `collection.bodySite` has CodeableConcept members such as `coding` and `text` directly under `bodySite`; in R6 those must be nested under `bodySite.concept`. R6 can also use `bodySite.reference` to BodyStructure, which has no base R4 equivalent at the same path.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Body site is clinically meaningful for pathology, microbiology, and other specimen workflows; mis-conversion can change the anatomical source of a result.

justification.inferredGoal: Support both coded body sites and references to modeled BodyStructure instances in the base resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `bodySite` as `CodeableConcept` and add a separate optional BodyStructure reference element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is well supported by the element comment: some collection sites need a specific `BodyStructure` instance or richer structured attributes. A sibling-reference design could have preserved old JSON, but it would create two base elements for the same anatomical site and require rules for when both are present. Because those tradeoffs are material, the CodeableReference change is probably justified, though not the only plausible design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking alternative would keep `Specimen.collection.bodySite` as `CodeableConcept` and add something like an optional `bodyStructure` reference for cases needing a modeled site instance. This preserves R4 instances and supports the core new use case, but it splits one clinical fact across two fields, complicates validation and search, and risks indefinite duplicate representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves coded R4 body sites, but introduces parallel coded and referenced site representations with consistency ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 type is CodeableConcept.
R6 type is CodeableReference with targetProfile BodyStructure.
CodeableReference has `concept` and `reference` children, so the JSON shape differs from CodeableConcept.
R6 describes when a BodyStructure reference should be used.

examples.examplesMd: The first transform is structural wrapping. The BodyStructure reference example cannot be represented in base R4 `Specimen.collection.bodySite` without an extension or out-of-band resource linkage.

findings.narrativeMd: The body-site path looks stable, but its datatype changed to `CodeableReference`. This is a classic hidden wire-format break: semantically similar coded content needs to be wrapped under `concept`, and R6 adds a reference form that R4 did not support in the base element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A populated R4 CodeableConcept at `collection.bodySite` will fail R6 validation because `coding` is no longer a direct child of the element. R6 BodyStructure references cannot round-trip to R4 without extension policy. Generated models will expose a different type and different accessors.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap old CodeableConcept values as `collection.bodySite.concept`. For R6 BodyStructure references, decide whether to dereference to a code, use the R4 bodySite extension mentioned by R4, or preserve the relationship in an implementation-specific extension. Include tests for coded body sites, text-only body sites, and BodyStructure references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: CodeableReference is well suited to the stated need, but it breaks existing JSON. A sibling reference would have been more compatible while less elegant and potentially harder to constrain. The chosen design favors model consistency over wire compatibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 changes `collection.bodySite` from a raw CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(BodyStructure). Existing coded body sites must be wrapped under `bodySite.concept`, and R6 references to BodyStructure cannot be represented in base R4 at the same path. The break is real, but the R6 goal of supporting a coded site or a modeled site instance is clinically reasonable, and sibling-field alternatives would split one anatomical fact across two fields.
keyEvidence: R4 `Specimen.collection.bodySite` is CodeableConcept 0..1 with body-site example binding.
R6 `Specimen.collection.bodySite` is CodeableReference 0..1 targeting BodyStructure with the same body-site value set for the concept arm.
R6 `StructureDefinition-CodeableReference.json` defines `concept` and `reference` children.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. The clinical importance of body site makes migration correctness important, but the maturity level does not make the compatibility break disproportionate by itself.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `bodySite.coding` or `bodySite.text` is not the R6 CodeableReference shape; R6 BodyStructure references create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A separate optional BodyStructure reference beside the old CodeableConcept would preserve R4 JSON, but it would create competing representations for the same collection site and require rules when both are present. CodeableReference is a coherent R6 design despite the wire-shape break.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the break is significant, but the less-breaking design has material modeling costs.

findings.title: Specimen.processing.additive changed from Reference(Substance) to CodeableReference(Substance or SubstanceDefinition)

oldState.summary: R4 additive was a repeating Reference limited to Substance.

semanticText.definition: Material used in the processing step.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required each processing additive to be a direct `Reference(Substance)` value.

newState.summary: R6 additive is a repeating CodeableReference targeting Substance or SubstanceDefinition.

semanticText.definition: Material used in the processing step.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can carry either a coded concept or a reference, and references may point to Substance or SubstanceDefinition. The reference, if used, is nested under the CodeableReference `reference` child.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `processing.additive` contain Reference fields directly in each array item. R6 expects CodeableReference items, so the reference must be nested. R6 can also carry a concept-only additive or a SubstanceDefinition reference, neither of which has an equivalent R4 base representation as `Reference(Substance)`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Processing additives such as fixatives or reagents can materially affect specimen interpretation. Dropping or misidentifying them can alter analytic context.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow additives to be represented by terminology concepts or substance definitions, not only Substance instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `processing.additive` as `Reference(Substance)` and add separate coded or definition-based additive element(s).
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of allowing additive concepts and `SubstanceDefinition` references is reasonable because an additive may be known by code or definition rather than by a concrete `Substance` instance. A less-breaking sibling-element design could cover many cases, but it would leave multiple same-resource representations of the additive fact. The material duplication and modeling inconsistency make the CodeableReference change probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatible alternative would keep the existing `processing.additive` reference shape and add separate optional fields for coded additives or substance definitions. That would preserve R4 instances, but it would require precedence and consistency rules when a reference and a code/definition both describe the same additive, and it would diverge from the single CodeableReference pattern used elsewhere in R6.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old references, but duplicates additive semantics and makes constraints and conversions more complex.

evidence.detail: R4 type is Reference with targetProfile Substance.
R6 type is CodeableReference with targetProfiles Substance and SubstanceDefinition.
CodeableReference represents the concept/reference alternatives using children named `concept` and `reference`.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 Reference can be wrapped under the CodeableReference `reference` child. Concept-only R6 additives or SubstanceDefinition references need a policy for R4 conversion.

findings.narrativeMd: `Specimen.processing.additive` kept its path and cardinality but changed datatype. That makes the change easy to miss in path-only diffs while still breaking populated instances and generated accessors.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A direct R4 Reference object in `processing.additive[]` is not a valid R6 CodeableReference. R6 content using the concept arm or SubstanceDefinition target cannot be represented as R4 `Reference(Substance)` without loss or extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap old references as `additive[].reference`. Decide whether concept-only R6 additives should become generated Substance resources, extensions, or be rejected for R4 export. Test conversions for Substance references, SubstanceDefinition references, and text-only concepts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The expressivity gain is clear, but a direct choice expansion or sibling element could have avoided changing the JSON shape of existing references. The R6 choice favors a standard CodeableReference pattern at the cost of compatibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `processing.additive` moved from direct Reference(Substance) values to CodeableReference values that can be a concept, a Substance reference, or a SubstanceDefinition reference. Direct R4 Reference JSON must be nested under the CodeableReference reference arm, so old instances and generated APIs break. The added expressivity is plausible for additives known by code or definition rather than an instantiated Substance.
keyEvidence: R4 `Specimen.processing.additive` is Reference(Substance) 0..*.
R6 `Specimen.processing.additive` is CodeableReference 0..* targeting Substance or SubstanceDefinition.
R6 `StructureDefinition-CodeableReference.json` defines separate `concept` and `reference` children.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. Processing additives can affect analytic interpretation, but the R6 expressivity gain is relevant enough that FMM does not push this to Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 array items with direct Reference fields are not the R6 CodeableReference shape; concept-only and SubstanceDefinition R6 additives are lossy to R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained the Reference(Substance) element and added sibling coded or definition-based additive elements. That would preserve old references but duplicate additive semantics and complicate precedence and constraints. The single CodeableReference design is probably worth the migration cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment.

findings.title: Specimen.subject semantics were narrowed to subject-of-record and R6 adds Specimen.focus for the actual collection source

oldState.summary: R4 subject represented where the specimen came from and targeted Patient, Group, Device, Substance, or Location.

semanticText.definition: Where the specimen came from. This may be from patient(s), from a location, or a sampling of a substance or a device.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 described `subject` as the source the specimen came from.

newState.summary: R6 subject is the subject of record, adds BiologicallyDerivedProduct and NutritionProduct targets, and adds focus for a different collection source.

semanticText.definition: The subject of record that the specimen is associated with... If the specimen is collected from an entity different from the subject of record, that entity should be recorded using Specimen.focus.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes `subject` a record-target field and uses new `Specimen.focus` for the entity actually collected from when that differs.

facts.newValue: BiologicallyDerivedProduct and Group may need to be conveyed as focus with patient as subject in specific cases.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 instances with allowed subject targets remain structurally valid in R6, but their interpretation can change if they used `subject` to mean the physical source rather than the subject of record. R6 instances using `focus`, `subject` targets BiologicallyDerivedProduct/NutritionProduct, or `focus` target RelatedPerson cannot round-trip to base R4 without extensions or semantic collapse.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Confusing subject-of-record with actual specimen source can associate results with the wrong patient, group, donor, fetus, animal, device, or environmental source.

justification.inferredGoal: Disambiguate record ownership from the entity actually sampled and support more subject/source scenarios.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `subject` as the collection source and add a distinct subject-of-record or source/focus element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 split between subject of record and actual collection source addresses real ambiguity for donor, fetus, animal, group, and biologically derived product scenarios. A less-breaking semantic design could preserve the R4 meaning of `subject`, but that would keep Specimen misaligned with the common FHIR use of `subject` as the record target. Because the alternative has significant semantic and interoperability tradeoffs, the change is probably justified, but not so unavoidable that the partial alternative should be ignored.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design would leave `Specimen.subject` meaning the entity from which the specimen came and add a separate subject-of-record element, or add a separate source/focus element without redefining `subject`. That would make old R4 data easier to interpret, but it would require implementers to learn resource-specific subject semantics and could make cross-resource record-target handling less consistent.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old semantics, but conflicts with broader FHIR `subject` conventions and adds record-target/source modeling complexity.

evidence.detail: R4 defines subject as where the specimen came from.
R6 defines subject as the subject of record and directs different collection sources to Specimen.focus.
R6 adds `Specimen.focus` for the entity from which the specimen was collected when different from subject.
R6 adds subject target profiles BiologicallyDerivedProduct and NutritionProduct.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates the R6 subject/focus split. R4 has only `subject`, so preserving both record subject and actual collection focus requires an extension or local convention.

findings.narrativeMd: The `subject` element did not just gain targets; its meaning changed from 'where the specimen came from' to 'subject of record', with the actual collection source moving to new `focus` when different. This is not a direct validation break for ordinary R4 specimens, but it is a semantic migration risk. Automated transforms cannot always know whether an old R4 subject was intended as record owner or physical source.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Most R4 `subject` references remain valid R6 references. The break is semantic and round-trip oriented: R6 can represent subject/focus pairs and new target types that base R4 cannot carry. Strict R6 validation will accept old target types but cannot validate that an old subject was semantically reinterpreted correctly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review use cases where specimens are collected from an entity associated with a patient or record target, such as donor material, fetus specimens, animal/environmental sources linked to a patient record, biologically derived products, and group/herd scenarios. Populate R6 `focus` when the collection source differs from the subject of record. For R4 export, define an extension or a policy for collapsing `focus` to `subject` with known information loss.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 split is clinically clearer and aligns `subject` with broader FHIR usage. A more backward-compatible but less conventional design would have kept the old source meaning and added a new record-subject field. The chosen approach requires migration review but improves long-term semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The structural target list mostly widens, but the meaning of `subject` changes from the source the specimen came from to the subject of record, with new `focus` holding a different actual source. That can be safety-significant for donor, fetus, group, animal, environmental, or product-associated specimens because a converter may need clinical or workflow context to decide whether an old R4 subject remains `subject` or becomes `focus` with a different record subject.
keyEvidence: R4 `Specimen.subject.definition` says where the specimen came from and targets Patient, Group, Device, Substance, or Location.
R6 `Specimen.subject.definition` says subject of record and directs different collection sources to `Specimen.focus`.
R6 adds `Specimen.focus` 0..1 Reference including RelatedPerson and the other source-like targets.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, but the affected element is central to associating specimen results with the correct record or source, so the safety relevance outweighs the modest maturity level.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: unchanged R4 instances may still validate, but their intended meaning can shift; R6 `focus` also creates R6-to-R4 semantic loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `subject` as the physical source and added a separate subject-of-record field, or added `focus` without redefining `subject`. That would preserve old semantics but keep Specimen less aligned with broader FHIR subject-as-record-target conventions. The design may be right, but the migration ambiguity is substantial enough to deserve attention.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment: the R6 split is well motivated, but the old-to-new semantic decision can be expert-dependent and safety-relevant.

findings.title: R6 adds Specimen.combined, Specimen.role, and Specimen.feature, which are not representable in base R4

oldState.summary: R4 had no base elements for pooled/grouped status, specimen role, or physical feature annotations.
oldState.narrativeMd: Comparable R4 content would need extensions, profiles, notes, or external workflow context.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional combined status, repeating role, and repeating feature backbone with mandatory type and description when used.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can state whether a specimen is grouped or pooled, declare workflow roles such as patient/control/calibrator, and describe highlighted physical features or landmarks. Each `feature` repetition must include both `type` and `description`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are additive for R4-to-R6 migration, so old instances are not invalidated. They are significant for R6-to-R4 conversion because base R4 has no equivalent fields for pooled/grouped status, workflow role, or structured physical feature annotations. R6 validation also requires both type and description inside each feature repetition.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Control/calibrator/patient roles and pooled/grouped status can affect laboratory interpretation and quality-control workflows; losing them on R4 export may be clinically or operationally material.

justification.inferredGoal: Add explicit support for specimen grouping, workflow roles, and annotated physical features.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: The R6 elements are optional additions that already preserve R4 instances; R4 extensions are downgrade mitigations, not a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `combined`, `role`, and `feature` add optional R6 expressivity for specimen grouping, workflow role, and physical feature annotations. Existing R4 instances are not invalidated by these additions, so the backward-compatible-alternative question is not applicable in the R4-to-R6 base-design sense. The remaining issue is R6-to-R4 export loss, which is a conversion concern rather than evidence that R6 should have used a different base shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed because the additions are optional. R4 cross-version extensions, profiles, or narrative degradation can mitigate downgrade loss, but those are migration/export strategies for older systems and should not be counted as backward-compatible base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No R4-to-R6 break needs a less-breaking alternative; avoiding the fields would only reduce R6 expressivity.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `Specimen.combined` as code 0..1 with required specimen-combined value set.
R6 combined codes are `grouped` and `pooled`.
R6 defines `Specimen.role` as CodeableConcept 0..*.
R6 role codes include patient, control specimen, calibrator, proficiency, replicate, and related roles.
R6 feature repetitions require both type and description with min=1.

feature.description: red ink on right lobe margin

examples.examplesMd: All shown fields are base R6 fields with no base R4 paths. An R4 export needs extensions, notes, or loss of structured data.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces several new specimen characterization fields. They do not break old R4 instances, but they create a real downgrade problem because R4 has no native place for pooled/grouped status, specimen role, or structured physical feature annotations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is unaffected unless a migration chooses to populate `feature` incompletely; R6 requires both `feature.type` and `feature.description`. R6-to-R4 conversion cannot preserve these fields in base R4 without extensions or text degradation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-consuming systems, define cross-version extensions for `combined`, `role`, and `feature`, or document intentional loss. For R6 validation, ensure each feature has both `type` and `description`. Tests should include pooled specimens, QC/control roles, and feature annotations with missing required children.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because these are optional additions, the R6 design is backward-compatible for R4-to-R6 and the R6-to-R4 loss is inherent to older-version export. No less disruptive R6 design is apparent beyond publishing standard cross-version extensions.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `combined`, `role`, and `feature` are optional R6 additions, so unchanged R4 specimens are not invalidated. The compatibility issue is downgrade-only: R6 can now express pooled/grouped status, workflow role, and feature annotations that base R4 cannot carry. That loss can matter for quality-control and interpretation workflows, but avoiding the fields would simply make R6 less expressive.
keyEvidence: R6 adds optional `Specimen.combined`, `Specimen.role`, and repeating `Specimen.feature`.
R6 `Specimen.feature.type` and `Specimen.feature.description` are both 1..1 when a feature is present.
Local code systems checked: `specimen-combined` has grouped/pooled; `specimen-role` includes patient, control specimen, calibrator, proficiency, and replicate roles.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. Because this is additive for R4-to-R6, FMM does not increase concern; possible downgrade loss is judged on workflow relevance instead.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: base R4 has no equivalent elements for grouped/pooled status, specimen role, or structured feature annotations.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed because the fields are optional and do not break old instances. Standard R4 extensions would help downgrades, but they are mitigation rather than an alternate R6 shape.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Not applicable alternative judgment: the downgrade loss is real, but it is not evidence that the R6 additions are problematic.

findings.title: R6 adds Specimen.collection.procedure and local invariant spm-1 forbids using it with collection.collector

oldState.summary: R4 had `collection.collector` but no `collection.procedure` element and no collector/procedure mutual-exclusion invariant.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 collection details could name a collector directly but could not link to the Procedure event that collected the specimen.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `collection.procedure` Reference(Procedure) and invariant spm-1: collector SHALL only be present if procedure is not present.

constraints.human: Specimen.collection.collector SHALL only be present if Specimen.collection.procedure is not present

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes collection Procedure linkage explicit, but treats the Procedure as the place to find performer details by preventing simultaneous `collector` and `procedure` on the Specimen.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances cannot already contain `collection.procedure`, so this is not an old-valid/new-invalid change by itself. It is still a migration and runtime risk: R4-to-R6 transforms that enrich specimens with a Procedure reference while also preserving `collector` will produce invalid R6, and R6 `collection.procedure` has no native R4 field.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily data consistency and workflow traceability, not direct clinical interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid duplicating collector/performer information on Specimen when a Procedure resource carries the collection event.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Unchanged R4 collector-only instances remain valid; making `spm-1` a warning would be a migration-friendly R6 policy choice, not preservation of invalidated R4 data.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The invariant has a reasonable consistency goal: if a Procedure represents the collection event, performer details should live there rather than also on `Specimen.collection.collector`. Because `collection.procedure` is new and optional, the error invariant does not by itself invalidate unchanged R4 instances. A warning-level rule would be friendlier for converters that enrich R4 data with Procedure links while preserving collector, but that is not a backward-compatible alternative for old base R4 instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: For R4-to-R6 base compatibility, no alternative is applicable because the constrained combination requires a new R6-only element. A softer warning or best-practice invariant could reduce R6 authoring and migration friction, but it would allow duplicated performer facts and is better characterized as an R6 modeling-policy tradeoff than as a less-breaking design for existing R4 content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No old R4 instance contains `collection.procedure`; the tradeoff is between strict R6 consistency and enriched-migration flexibility.

evidence.detail: R6 adds local error invariant spm-1 with expression `collection.collector.empty() or collection.procedure.empty()`.
R6 adds `collection.procedure` Reference(Procedure) 0..1.
R4 has no `collection.procedure` element.

examples.examplesMd: If a converter adds the Procedure link, it must not also emit `collection.collector` in the same R6 collection backbone.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 can point from the specimen collection details to the Procedure event, but enforces that the old direct `collector` field is absent when `procedure` is present. This does not invalidate unchanged R4 instances, but it can invalidate enriched migrations and R6 authoring workflows.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The validation effect is an R6 invariant failure, not an R4 data field removal: a Specimen with both `collection.collector` and `collection.procedure` fails R6 `spm-1`. R6 `collection.procedure` cannot be represented in base R4 Specimen except by extension or separate linkage.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When converting to R6, choose either direct `collection.collector` or `collection.procedure`. If a Procedure is available, move performer details to the Procedure and omit `collection.collector` from Specimen. For R4 export, decide whether to drop the Procedure link, use an extension, or derive `collector` from Procedure.performer where safe.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The invariant promotes consistency but could have been softer during transition. A warning would have accommodated legacy direct collector data while encouraging Procedure-based modeling.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `collection.procedure` and an error invariant forbidding it from coexisting with `collection.collector`. Since R4 had no `collection.procedure`, an unchanged R4 specimen with a collector remains valid in R6. The only failure case is an R6 authoring or enrichment choice that adds a Procedure link while also preserving collector, which is a modeling policy issue rather than an R4 compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 has `Specimen.collection.collector` but no `Specimen.collection.procedure`.
R6 adds `Specimen.collection.procedure` Reference(Procedure) 0..1.
R6 root constraint `spm-1` is error severity with expression `collection.collector.empty() or collection.procedure.empty()`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, and because no unchanged R4 instance is invalidated, maturity does not add practical concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: none: the invalid combination requires a new R6-only element; old R4 collector-only data is still valid.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-level invariant would be friendlier to enriched conversions, but it would also permit duplicated collector/performer facts when Procedure is the source of truth. Since this does not preserve any otherwise-invalid R4 instance, it is not a necessary less-breaking base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact assessment; the prior report correctly identifies the invariant but overstates it as an R4-to-R6 compatibility problem. The Not applicable alternative judgment is acceptable.

findings.title: R6 expands collection/processing workflow detail and reference targets beyond R4 representability

oldState.summary: R4 collection and processing had fewer workflow-detail fields and narrower collector/additive/time domains.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 collection collector targeted Practitioner or PractitionerRole; processing had no performer or device fields; processing time allowed dateTime or Period only.

newState.summary: R6 adds collection.device[x], processing.performer, processing.device[x], expands collection.collector targets, and adds Duration as a processing.time[x] choice.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can identify collection and processing devices, processing performers, non-practitioner collectors, and duration-only processing times. These additions are structurally valid R6 but do not map cleanly to base R4.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These changes mostly widen R6 and do not invalidate unchanged R4 content. The main risk is downgrade and runtime model divergence: R6 instances can use collector targets R4 disallows, device fields R4 lacks, processing performers R4 lacks, and `processing.timeDuration`, which R4 validators and generated models will not accept.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Device and performer information may be important for pre-analytic quality, chain-of-custody, and auditability. Duration-only processing time can matter for fixation and stabilization intervals.

justification.inferredGoal: Add structured workflow details for who or what collected and processed the specimen and support duration-only processing intervals.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: The workflow changes are optional additions or target/type widenings that preserve R4 instances; R4 extensions only mitigate R6-to-R4 export.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R6 adds optional workflow detail such as collection/processing devices, processing performer, broader collector targets, and `Duration` processing times. These changes do not make old R4 instances invalid, and widened targets preserve the old target set. The compatibility burden is primarily downgrade and bidirectional conversion policy, so the backward-compatible-alternative question is not applicable to the R6 base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the added fields and widened domains are optional. R4 extensions, derived Procedure/Provenance links, or constrained profiles can help older systems consume R6 information, but those are conversion mitigations rather than alternate R6 base designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No R4-to-R6 break needs a less-breaking alternative; avoiding the fields would sacrifice useful R6 workflow detail.

evidence.detail: R6 adds Organization, Patient, and RelatedPerson as collector targets.
R6 adds collection device choice with CodeableConcept, Reference(Device), and canonical(DeviceDefinition).
R6 adds processing performer.
R6 adds processing device choice.
R6 adds Duration to processing.time[x].

examples.examplesMd: Every highlighted field or target in the example is valid in R6 but either absent or outside the allowed target/type domain in R4.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds substantially richer collection and processing workflow detail. This is not a forward validation break, but it matters for systems that must emit R4, maintain shared generated models, or evaluate FHIRPath across versions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 validators will reject R6-only fields such as `collection.device[x]`, `processing.performer`, `processing.device[x]`, and `processing.timeDuration`. R4 also rejects newly allowed collector target types such as Organization, Patient, and RelatedPerson. Forward migration is safe if the new fields are not populated or are populated according to R6 choice naming.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For downgrade, decide whether to use extensions, map device/performer facts into Provenance or Procedure resources, or intentionally omit them. For `processing.timeDuration`, consider whether a duration can be converted into a Period only if an anchor time is available; otherwise preserve with an extension. Update generated models and FHIRPath expressions for the new choice names and target domains.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: These are optional R6 expressivity improvements, so the primary compatibility burden is on cross-version conversion. Avoiding them would reduce data quality; standard cross-version extensions would be the best compatibility support for R4 ecosystems.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens collection and processing workflow detail with optional device fields, a processing performer, broader collector targets, and Duration as a processing time choice. These changes preserve the old R4 domain for forward migration, but R6 instances using the new details cannot be cleanly exported to base R4. That can matter for chain-of-custody or pre-analytic quality records, yet the fields are useful R6 expressivity rather than avoidable breakage.
keyEvidence: R4 `collection.collector` targets Practitioner or PractitionerRole; R6 adds Organization, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R6 adds `collection.device[x]`, `processing.performer`, and `processing.device[x]`.
R4 `processing.time[x]` allows dateTime or Period; R6 also allows Duration.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. Because the changes are optional additions or widenings, FMM does not create a redesign concern; the remaining issue is downgrade policy.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R4 validators and models cannot carry the new device, performer, collector-target, or processing Duration representations without extensions or external resources.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is apparent because old R4 content remains in-domain. R4 extensions, Procedure/Provenance mappings, or documented loss are downgrade mitigations rather than reasons to omit the R6 fields.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Not applicable alternative judgment: the conversion burden is real for bidirectional systems, but it is proportionate to the added workflow detail.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R6 `StructureDefinition-Specimen.json` is present at the expected path. Canonical URL, id/name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag match R4; status changed from draft to active but that is not an instance-breaking identity change.

No existing local R4 element had its min increased or max decreased at the same path. Material cardinality effects are limited to new R6 content such as required `container.device[x]` when `container` is present and required children of new `feature`; these are covered in findings.

No type removals were found for `collection.collected[x]` or `collection.fastingStatus[x]`. Material local type replacements/additions are covered for `collection.bodySite`, `processing.additive`, `processing.time[x]`, and the container/device/workflow elements.

Stable reference paths such as `parent` and `request` did not narrow. Target expansions and R6-only targets for `subject`, `focus`, `collector`, `processing.performer`, and device choices are covered as R6-to-R4 representability risks.

No required local binding was found to remove status codes. `Specimen.status` appears code-stable; `Specimen.condition` weakened from extensible to example; processing/container/device binding changes are covered where they affect changed elements. Full terminology expansions were not available.

The only material local new invariant identified is `spm-1` on collection collector/procedure. Inherited `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension constraint expression/source differences were excluded by the base-artifact scope rule.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value additions/removals were identified on Specimen elements.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex constraints with material R4/R6 differences were identified.
No local Specimen business element changed `isModifier`. Inherited `modifierExtension` details are out of scope.

No retained local business element showed a material summary flag reversal. Removed summary elements such as `accessionIdentifier` and `container.identifier` are covered by element-removal findings. Inherited `modifierExtension` summary changes are out of scope.
No local slicing changes were identified in the Specimen StructureDefinitions.
Resource type remains `Specimen`. Serialization impacts are local property removals/renames and datatype shape changes, especially CodeableReference and R6 choice elements, covered in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Specimen.condition binding strength decreased from extensible to example
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Weakening an extensible binding to an example binding does not make previously valid R4 instances invalid in R6; it relaxes terminology expectations rather than tightening them.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Profiles or validators that relied on base R4's extensible binding may need to carry that expectation explicitly in local profiles if they still want it enforced.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Specimen.status value set version changed but codes and meanings are stable in local CodeSystems
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both R4 and R6 bind `Specimen.status` required to the same canonical value set, and the local complete CodeSystems contain the same four codes with the same definitions: `available`, `unavailable`, `unsatisfactory`, and `entered-in-error`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The ValueSet version suffix changes from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`; terminology servers or generated enums that key on version should verify configuration even though the code set appears unchanged.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Specimen.receivedTime wording now says receipt by the testing laboratory
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element path, cardinality, and `dateTime` type are unchanged, so no wire-format or validation break was found.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems using Specimen outside laboratory testing should review whether the R6 wording narrows intended use from generic receipt for processing/testing to receipt by a testing laboratory.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active while canonical identity stayed stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, abstract flag, and baseDefinition remain the same. The status maturation does not invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance or maturity filters may treat the R6 ballot resource differently because `status` is active rather than draft.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Several local Specimen elements now use CodeableReference. The datatype's own behavior and cross-version extension strategy should be assessed in its datatype report, while this report covers the local path-level consequences.
R6 container and workflow modeling depends on Device and DeviceDefinition. Container migration quality depends on how old inline container fields map to those resources.
Inherited dom-* constraints, language binding, and modifierExtension summary/text changes were intentionally excluded from local Specimen findings and should be owned by base artifact reports.
Accession identifier typing, container device mapping, processing procedure-to-method terminology, and R6-only roles/features would benefit from official or project-specific cross-version maps.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 Specimen diff or committee rationale was available locally. Structural findings are still high confidence, but justification and backward-compatible alternative analysis are partly inferred.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official FHIR change notes, Jira tickets, or ballot reconciliation notes for Specimen.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Local ValueSet compose definitions and small CodeSystems were inspected, but full terminology-server expansions were not run for SNOMED-based body-site, processing-method, container-device, or processing-device value sets.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run version-pinned terminology expansions and compare code coverage, especially for old v2-0373 processing procedure codes versus the R6 SNOMED method set.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official cross-version ConceptMaps were found for the main structural remodels: accessionIdentifier to typed identifier, inline container fields to device modeling, processing procedure to method, or CodeableReference wrapping/unwrapping.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use official HL7 cross-version maps if available, or define project-specific maps and extension policies for lossy downgrade cases.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The package did not provide full narrative Specimen specification pages for additional explanatory text beyond the StructureDefinitions and generated terminology artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare the published R4 and R6 Specimen pages, examples, and notes sections.

suggestedMigrationBacklogGroups: R6-to-R4 extension strategy for new Specimen fields
